A common four-swimmer relay order used is second-fastest, third-fastest, slowest, then fastest (anchor) [d182796s1p0].
An alternative relay order sometimes used places the slowest swimmer second (second-fastest, slowest, third-fastest, fastest) or arranges swimmers from slowest to fastest [d182796s1p0].
A takeover with a rolling start by the second, third, or fourth swimmer can save approximately 0.6–1.0 seconds compared to a regular start because the starting swimmer may already be in motion [d182796s1p0].
Relay times are typically 2–3 seconds faster than the sum of the individual swimmers' best times, attributable in part to takeover advantages and team effects [d182796s1p0].
The medley relay stroke order is backstroke, breaststroke, butterfly, and freestyle, and the freestyle relay leg cannot use the first three strokes [d182796s1p0].
